avoid.pattern: Vendor newsrooms, launch posts, CEO interviews for capability, deployment or schedule claims
avoid.why: The claimant benefits; 'deployed', 'net energy', 'AI-designed' get redefined. Lead only; cite with an independent eval, regulator record or on-record customer.

avoid.pattern: SEO explainers and aggregator sites summarising FDA counts, state AI laws, IEA figures
avoid.why: Second-hand, undated, frequently wrong on counts and dates. Go to the primary they summarise.

avoid.pattern: Prediction-market odds (Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold) or Metaculus medians as sole evidence
avoid.why: Thin liquidity, resolution mismatch, reflexive with news; they are forecasts not observations. Use as a calibration flag (>15-point divergence) and cite the underlying event.

avoid.pattern: Automated incident or news feeds (OECD AIM, news digests, Climate Reanalyzer daily values)
avoid.why: Duplicates and misclassification; leads to the underlying advisory or dataset only.

avoid.pattern: Advocacy groups on their own cause (BIEN, 4 Day Week Global, FLI index, industry associations on timelines)
avoid.why: Selection effects and member self-reports. Use to discover; confirm in statute, gazette or statistical office.

avoid.pattern: Consulting 'state of AI' surveys (McKinsey, Gartner, WEF) for adoption or displacement numbers
avoid.why: Self-selected executive samples, lead-gen framing, incomparable across years. Use Census BTOS, Fed notes, BLS, NY Fed.
They are forecasts like this one; compare, never cite as evidence.
Follow their citations to the primary.

avoid.pattern: Paywalled press as the only source for a fact
avoid.why: Unverifiable to readers; find the primary document, else cite and mark 'paywalled'.

avoid.pattern: Single-month temperature records, single-day prices, single-benchmark SOTA claims
avoid.why: Noise; use 12-month means, monthly averages, multi-benchmark indices.
UN WPP, BLS, Epoch all revise; cite edition and access date.

rules: One primary or it did not happen: a probability moves only on a document from the measuring institution, regulator, legislature or an independent evaluator; press and vendor posts are leads that must resolve to such a document, else they go in the changelog body, not in sources.

A single vendor claim is a signal, never a resolution: it may move a reading by at most 0.1 or a probability by at most 2 points, only when specific (units, dates, customers), and the history entry says 'vendor claim, unverified'; two vendors saying the same thing are still one claim.

Independent evaluation beats self-report and the stricter metric beats the looser: METR/AISI/Epoch over lab benchmarks; regulator or grid-operator records over announcements; BLS/NY Fed over company statements.

Measure against the forecast's own definition: restate the line's test before citing (e.g. 'net electricity to a grid' = metered export confirmed by the ISO or utility); a source answering a different question does not count.
Paywalled primaries are citable (DOI/URL, title, date, exact sentence in history.reason); paywalled press only when no underlying document exists, marked 'paywalled' in the history entry.
Prediction-market moves count only with a named cause: flag a market diverging more than 15 points from a line, find the event behind it, and cite the event's source, never the price.
Cite datasets by edition and access date: 'Publisher, Dataset (revision), accessed YYYY-MM-DD, URL'; observed points in metrics.json carry the edition in their note.
One month is weather, twelve months is a reading: cite running annual or multi-benchmark figures for warming, prices, hiring and capability; a record month alone cannot move a probability.
Conflicting primaries: record both numbers in the history entry and lean on the slower-moving, more conservative one.

Resolving a line (happened, partial, early, late, missed) needs at least two independent primaries, or one primary plus an institutional or peer-reviewed confirmation, plus a date, all in history.sources.

Only cite pages you actually opened: for bot-blocked hosts (BLS, CISA, congress.gov, OECD, IEA, CDC, NCSL, GAO) use the registry's alternative host or search-then-fetch route; if it still fails, do not cite it and leave a note for the desktop run.
Each sourced history entry says what the source would have had to show to move the line the other way.
Refresh the registry quarterly: moved pages and dead links go in sources.json; a source failing twice in a row is demoted or replaced with a changelog note.
